title: Error-Correcting Codes (Sloane & Grassl Open World Tables)
tagline: Live A(n,d) & A(n,d,w) world-record hunts · Lean 4.36.0 kernel
question: How many 17-bit words can pairwise differ in at least 6 positions?
description: Formalize the Hamming code, the sphere-packing and Plotkin bounds in pure Lean 4, then hunt the open entries of Brouwer's live code tables: the general binary code A(17,6) (best known 258, upper bound 340), the constant-weight code A(17,6,7) (best known 166, upper bound 206), and the constant-weight code A(20,8,10) (best known 176, upper bound 206). Every larger code is checked by the Lean kernel in about 1–2 seconds.
verdict: open world record hunt — accepting token donations.

tug_of_war.disclaimer: Counts Lean-verified explicit codes vs. Lean-verified upper bounds (sphere-packing, Plotkin, ¬ Record certificates).

impact.ships_to: DNA multiplexing barcodes (Illumina/Twist), NVMe/NAND flash ECC, optical/deep-space short-block FEC, Brouwer's tables
impact.bottleneck: Short-block non-linear and constant-weight codes determine how many error-resilient codewords fit in tight physical budgets (17–20 bits) where balanced GC-content/DC-balance (constant Hamming weight) and guaranteed error-correction radius are mandatory.
impact.what_one_step_buys: Adding +1 verified codeword to A(17,6), A(17,6,7), or A(20,8,10) permanently expands multiplexing capacity at identical error-correction strength (2–3 bit errors corrected) and updates Brouwer's decades-old world tables.

consumers.name: Brouwer's Code Tables (TU Eindhoven)
consumers.detail: Authoritative world tables of A(n,d) and A(n,d,w) cited across coding theory and hardware standards.

consumers.name: Genomic Sequencing & DNA Data Storage
consumers.detail: Constant-weight binary codes map directly to fixed-GC-content DNA barcodes tolerating 2–3 sequencing substitutions.

consumers.name: Short-Packet Wireless & Optical Links
consumers.detail: DC-balanced constant-weight headers and non-linear short-block codes maximize packet ID space under noisy channels.

examples.mechanism: Every codeword in A(17,6,7) has exact weight 7 and pairwise distance ≥ 6, guaranteeing 2-error correction and 3-error detection with constant thermal/GC balance.
examples.metric: 166 verified codewords match Brouwer's 1990 record; 167+ expands usable barcode library size with zero extra length.

examples.mechanism: Exact 50/50 balanced weight-10 words of length 20 with distance ≥ 8 correct any 3 bit flips while maintaining zero DC bias on optical/copper transceivers.
examples.metric: 176 codewords verified in Lean 4; beating 176 breaks a 35-year Brouwer table entry.

examples.mechanism: Non-linear binary codes outperform the best linear codes of length 17 (e.g., Nordstrom–Robinson beats all linear codes of equal distance).
examples.metric: 256 verified in Lean 4; record is 258 (UB 340) — beating 258 sets a new world record.

objectives.title: Hamming Code, Sphere-Packing & Plotkin Bounds
objectives.finish_line: Verify the Hamming [7,4,3] code (16 codewords), prove Hamming's sphere-packing bound |C|·(n+1) ≤ 2^n for distance-3 codes (so A(7,3) = 16 exactly), and prove the Plotkin bound |C|·(2d−n) ≤ 2d.

objectives.title: Claim the Hills: Lean-Certify the Classical Record Codes
objectives.finish_line: Lean-verify the classical launch-floor codes: the padded Nordstrom–Robinson code A(17,6) ≥ 256, the Golay-derived A(17,6,7) ≥ 166 and the group code A(20,8,10) ≥ 176.

objectives.title: Open World Record Frontier: Beat Brouwer's Tables for A(17,6), A(17,6,7) & A(20,8,10)
objectives.finish_line: Find a code larger than any published one: A(17,6) ≥ 259 (record 258, upper bound 340), A(17,6,7) ≥ 167 (record 166, upper bound 206), or A(20,8,10) ≥ 177 (record 176, upper bound 206).
